Fault surfaces v1 from catalog v5.1

2026-11-25. Plane-based fault surfaces refitted on catalog v5.1 (NonLinLoc in the 3D model v0.3.1, re-timed picks), compared surface by surface with v0 (catalog v4). Code: workflow/07_faults/v1_*.py on branch analysis/v51-faults. Private working product.

Summary

  • 142 surfaces (99 steep, dip ≥ 45°) from 101,296 well-constrained events (v0: 141 surfaces from 76,281 events). 64,272 events (63% of the fit set) are fit members of a surface (v0: 53,291, 70%).
  • Every located event (171,719; 623 rows without a hypocentre left out) has an assignment: 64,272 fit members, 12,638 assigned to one surface within twice their combined uncertainty and within 10 km, 26,266 compatible with two or more surfaces (ambiguous, not assigned), 64,093 on no surface, 3,313 non-earthquakes (event_flag) and 1,137 events of surfaces removed for their weekday-daytime timing.
  • Against v0 (by shared fit members): matched 50, new 39, split 23, split and merged 20, merged 10 among the v1 surfaces; of the 141 v0 surfaces: matched 50, merged 25, lost 23, split and merged 20, dispersed 13, split 10.
  • Literature: 19 v1 surfaces carry a v0 match unchanged, 84 carry one marked for re-check (split, merged or moved), and 39 are new and need a literature check (fault_surfaces_v1_literature_todo.csv).
  • Uncertainty. Median sigma_total of the surface position is 0.59 km (10th-90th percentile 0.23-1.07 km). Tier A catalog errors match the scatter of events about their surfaces; tier B and C errors are larger than it (median |normal residual| / event error 0.40 over all members, 0.67 if the errors described the scatter).
Findings to read first
  • Fewer events on a fault than v0, for a stated reason. 142 surfaces hold 64,272 fit members. The first v1 run, with the v0 code unchanged, found 192 planes, 75,409 of 101,296 events (74 %), but 26 of its planes ended flatter than 30° after reassignment, as 24 of v0's 141 did. With the dip rule applied in every reassignment pass, flat clouds no longer pass as faults; the share on a fault drops most in Puget (v0 61 %, v1 34 %) and onshore, where v0 kept low-dip layers (PU001, PU002, ON002).
  • Matched surfaces moved with their events. 50 v0 surfaces have one v1 counterpart. Their centroids moved a median 5.9 km horizontally and +2.3 km in depth, close to the median v4 → v5.1 depth shift of their events (+2.1 km). Strike changed by a median 23° (normals 26° apart); 17 kept their strike within 10° and 14 turned by more than 45°. The other v0 surfaces: 25 merged, 10 split, 20 in mixed groups, 13 dispersed over several v1 surfaces, 23 lost; 39 v1 surfaces are new.
  • Blanco depths moved down; rectangles reach 30-50 km. The events of the v0 Blanco Ridge strand (BL003a, 3,440 events) went from a median 9.2 km (v4) to 16.5 km (v5.1). Against the Lange et al. (2026) OBS catalog, v5.1 tier A-C Blanco Ridge events are a median 2.9 km deeper with a 90th percentile of +13 km, Gorda Depression +5.6 km (+16.6 km) (catalog paired_v5.1.md). This deep tail sets the bottom of the Blanco rectangles. 4 Blanco surfaces are centred below 20 km (v1_BL009, v1_BL012, v1_BL015, v1_BL016), and one deep surface under the Cascadia Depression with only 18 depth-ok events was removed as an artefact, as v0 did for three.
  • The Cascadia Depression N-S faults are not recovered as N-S planes. The events of v0 BL005, BL008 and BL012 (N-S normal faults, high-confidence literature match) keep their N-S map elongation in v5.1 (azimuths 10°, 177°, 4°). The v1 detection first fitted a plane striking 121° and dipping 68° (2,357 events, 64 km long) through the dense cluster and on to the western Blanco Ridge (v1_BL004), then split the rest (BL005: v1_BL004 36%, v1_BL006 25%, v1_BL012 6%; BL008: v1_BL004 47%, v1_BL006 24%, v1_BL012 5%; BL012: v1_BL004 29%, v1_BL010 24%, v1_BL006 13%). This comes from the detection order, not from the relocation. A fit restricted to the Cascadia Depression is needed before v1 is used there.
  • Deep events under Mount St. Helens are probably a recurring non-earthquake signal. Surface v1x_06 (39 events at 60 km under the volcano) was removed for its timing (64% weekday daytime). In the Mount St. Helens box, 331 of 7,471 located events are deeper than 30 km (30-118 km; tiers A 1, B 3, C 118, D 209; median sig_z 17 km although stations are a few km away), and 22 of them occur on Wednesdays between 19:14 and 19:20 UTC (on Tuesdays at that time: 0). A weekly repeat at the same minute points to a test or calibration signal, not earthquakes. This is a catalog problem to pass on, not a fault.
  • The 2012 Brookings swarm is now at about 52 km. v1_GO022 (39 events, 33 in 2012; v0 GO020, a candidate new structure at about 12 km) lies at 42-65 km in v5.1, against a median 20 km in v4; depth_quality is ok for 100% of its events, median sig_z 7 km, nearest station 45 km. Slab2 puts the slab top at about 15-20 km there. This depth needs a check against ComCat and the OBS data before the surface is interpreted.
  • Endeavour-Explorer surfaces sit at 30-60 km (5 surfaces) on events whose depths the catalog marks as unconstrained (ridge regions). Their map traces can be used; their depths and dips cannot.
  • Catalog errors and scatter. Tier A errors describe the scatter of events about their surface (median |residual|/error 0.77, 0.67 expected). For tiers B and C the errors are larger than the scatter (0.49, 0.30). The RMS residual is 1.1-1.2 km for every tier, close to what the selection tolerance allows (about 2.3 km for vertical faults), so the zone widths are set by the method more than by the locations.

Data and event selection

Fit set (PI choice of 2026-11-25): tiers A-C located by NonLinLoc, without floor_limited, far_only and deep_pass events, without ComCat explosions, quarry blasts and other non-earthquakes and without the Texada quarry_blast_likely events. Axial Seamount stays out as in v0 (published fault maps there are better). Rows are removed by the first rule that applies:

RuleEvents

Per-event error: sigma_h = sqrt((h_min² + h_max²)/2) / 1.515 (68 % semi-axes to one sigma, the convention of the tomography code; the catalog has no ellipse azimuth) and sigma_z = sig_z. Fit-set medians: sigma_h 1.35 km, sigma_z 3.59 km; by tier A 0.71/1.17 km, B 1.19/2.37 km, C 1.90/5.47 km. Depths are km below sea level.

Method

  1. Detection: the v0 method and parameters (fault_surfaces_planes.py): sequential local RANSAC with growth, tolerance 1.5 × sqrt((1.5 km |n_h|)² + (3 km n_z)²), ≥ 30 events, planarity ≤ 0.5, dip ≥ 30°, k-planes reassignment, merging. One change: the dip rule is also applied after every reassignment pass (in v0, 24 of the 141 surfaces ended flatter than 30° after reassignment).
  2. Blanco strands (rule of split_strands.py, now automatic): steep Blanco planes within 35° of plate motion and mostly outside the Cascadia Depression box are re-searched as map-view strands in the three v0 pools (west, Blanco Ridge, Gorda Depression). Overlapping parallel strands stay apart only if Ashman's D > 2 overall and in every year where both have ≥ 15 events; pairs whose depth offset would need a single fault dipping ≥ 60° are merged (offset follows depth, the reason v0 merged its two 'deeper band' strands).
  3. Rectangles as v0 (2-98 % extent along strike and dip + 0.5 km, plane or gentle quadratic by BIC, 1 km mesh).
  4. Uncertainty per surface: bootstrap of the members (100 draws), location Monte Carlo moving every member by its own catalog error (100 draws; v0 used nominal 1.5/1.5/3 km), model choice, combined; strike/dip intervals from each; centroid spread; stability over the four detection reruns of v0 (Jaccard overlap).
  5. Screening: surfaces with ≥ 60 % of their events on weekdays 08-17 local time are removed (quarry blasts or other non-earthquake signals; catalog average 28 %); Blanco surfaces centred deeper than 25 km with fewer than 30 depth-ok events are removed as deep artefacts (v0 removed three such surfaces after its literature check); a final dip < 30° would also remove a surface (none left after the dip rule in detection).
  6. Assignment of every located event: distance d to the surface (normal offset inside the rectangle, plus the in-plane distance outside it); z = d / sqrt(s_e² + s_s² + W²) with s_e the event's error along that direction, s_s the surface's median sigma_total and W its zone width once the member errors are taken out. Compatible: z ≤ 2 and d ≤ 10 km. Assigned: exactly one compatible surface; ambiguous: two or more.
  7. Comparison with v0: v0 members (catalog v4 IDs, the same as v5.1 IDs) against v1 fit members. A v0 and a v1 surface are linked when they share ≥ 15 events and these are ≥ 50 % of the v0 surface's re-found events, or ≥ 50 % of the v1 surface's events that were on a v0 surface, or ≥ 30 % of both. Connected groups: matched (1-1), split (1-n), merged (n-1), split and merged, new, lost. Removed v1 surfaces take part in the links, so a v0 surface whose events now form a removed surface is reported as lost with that reason.

Blanco strands

12 strands replace 21 Blanco planes. 8 overlapping pairs were merged because their depth offset would need a single fault dipping 62-80° (the Blanco faults are near vertical, so the offset is read as depth-dependent location error, as for v0's 'deeper band' strands), and 2 because the separation failed in at least one year. Without the depth rule, v1 would keep more parallel strands; the table lists every merge.

Two Blanco Ridge strands south of the main strand v1_BL005, v1_BL009 (877 events, 32% depth-ok, centroid 23 km), v1_BL015 (257 events, 25% depth-ok, centroid 23 km), pass the depth test because the test uses depth-ok events only, which sit at the same median depth as v1_BL005. Most of their events have unconstrained depths. They are where v0's merged 'deeper band' was, and need the same check before being read as separate faults.

Uncertainties

Per surface (1 sigma normal to the surface, median over vertices): sigma_total 0.59 km (10th-90th percentile 0.23-1.07), of which location Monte Carlo 0.46, bootstrap 0.21 and model choice 0.16 km. The location term uses the catalog errors, which for tiers B and C are larger than the scatter, so it is an upper bound. It treats errors as independent between events; errors shared by nearby events (velocity model, station terms) move a whole surface and are not in it; the v0 → v1 shift of matched surfaces (median 5.9 km horizontally) shows their size between two location runs. Strike and dip: bootstrap 68 % interval widths, median 2.0° and 3.1°; with the location Monte Carlo 5.7° and 7.0°. Centroid: 0.72 km horizontally and 0.31 km in depth (bootstrap). 49 of 142 surfaces are stable (median Jaccard ≥ 0.5 over the four detection reruns; v0: 50 of 141). Per tier:

Checks and limits

  • 14 surfaces have mesh vertices above the ground or seafloor (GMT earth_relief 01m): the rectangle is extrapolated 0.5 km and to the 2-98 % extent of the members; no hypocentre is above the surface (catalog v5.1). Listed in the summary (n_vertices_above_surface).
  • 37 surfaces have fewer than half of their events with depth_quality ok (Blanco outside the 2012-13 OBS deployment, Gorda far from stations): their dips and depth extents rest on poorly constrained depths; dip_depth_ok and events_depth_ok_2pct_km/98pct_km give the same from the ok events only.
  • Rectangles are crude: one plane or gentle quadratic over the 2-98 % extent of the members. Curved or branching faults come out as several rectangles.
  • No relative relocation: the scatter about the surfaces (RMS about 1.2 km) is still wider than double-difference catalogs show for the same faults.
  • ComCat focal mechanisms were not used to steer or check the surfaces (PI rule).
  • The mesh vertex elevations (surface_elev_km) use GMT earth_relief 01m, not the merged GMRT surface of the catalog.

Proposed decisions

  1. Dip rule in every reassignment pass (v1_detect.reassign_dip): a plane flatter than 30° after reassignment is dropped and its events go back to the other planes. v0 checked the dip only at detection and merging; 24 of its 141 surfaces ended flatter. Effect on v5.1: 192 → 161 planes, 74 % → 67 % of the fit set on a plane.
  2. Event selection: 'deep-pass-only' read as deep_pass = True (83 tier A-C events); anss_other_event and anss_sonic_boom also excluded as non-earthquakes (1 event); Axial left out as in v0; the 2 loc_source comcat rows (tier U) are assigned with nominal errors of 1.5 km (horizontal) and 3 km (depth).
  3. Per-event error: sigma_h = sqrt((h_min² + h_max²)/2) / 1.515, isotropic (no ellipse azimuth in the catalog); sigma_z = sig_z.
  4. Blanco strands made automatic: parents are steep Blanco planes within 35° of 111° with under half of their events in the Cascadia Depression box (-128.82 to -128.60 E, 43.74 to 43.88 N); events in that box are kept out of the strand pools; per-year Ashman D test (2 merges); pairs merged when their depth-ok median depths would need a single fault dipping ≥ 60° (8 merges; v0 merged two such pairs by judgement).
  5. Screening: surfaces with ≥ 60 % of events on weekdays 08-17 local time removed (9; their 1,137 events are marked and never assigned); Blanco surfaces centred deeper than 25 km with < 30 depth-ok events removed as deep artefacts (1).
  6. Assignment: compatible when z = d / sqrt(s_e² + s_s² + W²) ≤ 2 and d ≤ 10 km; assigned only when exactly one surface is compatible, otherwise 'ambiguous' with the two nearest listed. Without the 10 km cap and the uniqueness condition, events with errors of 10-15 km were 'compatible' with surfaces up to 70 km away.
  7. v0 comparison: link when ≥ 15 shared fit members that are ≥ 50 % of either side, or ≥ 30 % of both; literature carried unchanged only for matched surfaces with normals within 25° and centroids within 10 km; all other carried matches marked 're-check'.
  8. Surface IDs: v1_<region><nnn> (v0 region boxes, numbered by size); removed surfaces v1x_nn.
  9. Not done here, proposed as next steps: a fit restricted to the Cascadia Depression; a check of v1_BL009/v1_BL015 against the OBS-era depths; passing the Mount St. Helens weekly deep events and the Brookings swarm depth to the catalog owner.

In the worktree, data/catalog_v5/v5.1_analysis/faults/: fault_surfaces_v1_summary.csv (parameters, flags, carried literature), _uncertainty.csv, _rectangles.geojson (four corners per surface), _members.csv (fit members), _assignment.csv.gz (every located event), _assignment_by_region.csv, _selection.csv, _removed.csv and _removed_members.csv, _strand_separation.csv, _strand_merges.csv, _traces.csv, _v0_pairs.csv (every linked v0-v1 pair), _v0_status.csv (every v0 surface), _v0_comparison.csv (every v1 surface, with literature), _literature_todo.csv (new surfaces), the PNG figures and this report. On /wd1/mdenolle_data/catalog_v5/v5.1_analysis/faults/: fault_surfaces_v1.geojson (1 km triangle mesh, CRESCENT CFM layout), _vertices.csv.gz (per-vertex sigmas), _ensemble.csv.gz (100 draws per vertex), _assignment.csv.gz, work/ (detection runs, logs, member residuals) and RESUME.md.
